_comment: Indonesian personal data and secrets, as regular expressions with checks. `type` is what a match is masked as ([NIK_1]); `group` is the part that is the value (a label before it isn't); `validator` names a check in validators.py; `allow` lists values that never match (public test card numbers). Order matters where two patterns can match the same text: the earlier one wins. tests/fixtures.json is the behaviour, case by case.

patterns._comment: Family card (Kartu Keluarga) number after its label. Before id_nik: a KK number has the same shape as a NIK.
Passport number after its label: one or two letters and 6-7 digits (Indonesian passports: a letter and 7 digits).
BPJS Kesehatan / Ketenagakerjaan card number after the word BPJS, with up to three words between (BPJS Kesehatan no., bpjs aku).
Driving licence (SIM) number after its label (12-14 digits). Case-sensitive SIM: the word, not a SIM card (whose numbers are 19-20 digits anyway).

A number after the NPWP label: the old 15 digits written without dots, or the 16-digit NPWP used since 2024 (an individual's NIK, or 0 + the old 15 digits for a company). Before id_nik, so a labelled 16-digit number counts as an NPWP.
16 digits, also written in groups (3174 0912 0388 0004, 317409-120388-0004); the validator checks province and birth date
A number labelled NIK/KTP that isn't a valid 16-digit NIK (a typo, a digit missing): still someone's ID. `group` 1 is the number, so masking leaves the label.
A village or kampung address that starts with its name and RT/RW (Dusun Krajan RT 002/RW 003); the rest (Desa, Kec., Kab.) is added by the address extension in detect.py.
A firm named after its partners (KAP Budi Santoso, Hamid & Rekan): the whole name, so no partner is left visible. Capitalised names and a capitalised 'Rekan' only: 'saya & rekan kerja' is not a firm.
Indonesian mobile numbers: 08.., +62 8.., 62 8.., grouped with spaces, dots or dashes. The check counts 10-13 digits once written with a leading 0.

A bank account or virtual account number after its label (no. rek., rekening, norek, account no., a/c, VA), with up to three words between them (rek gaji Mandiri, rekening BSI nomor). Bare 9-17 digit numbers are too common to mask without the label.

An account number straight after a bank's name, with no label (ditransfer ke BCA 3376106017). Bank names are matched as written (BCA, not bca), so ordinary words don't trigger it; the check wants 9-17 digits.
Private network addresses (10/8, 172.16/12, 192.168/16): internal systems. Masked at any count; three or more in one message is a finding (a log or a network map).
Internal server names (.internal, .local, .corp, .lan, .intranet, .intra, .localdomain). Masked at any count; three or more is a finding.
